dependency: The preferred procedure treats sustained 900 rpm stirring until three successive five-second side-image spread checks are at most 4 percent as necessary for uniformity. Break that dependency by using a fresh recipe at a commanded 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, stopping regardless of side-image spread, with no subsequent stirring or feedback-driven restart before depth sampling at second 120. Repeat this fixed intervention within the six-trial session limit; optical checks are recorded but do not control operation.

predictions.account: Hypothesis: fixed lower-speed bulk mixing can satisfy the bounded sample criterion; sustained 900 rpm and optical stability are unnecessary in this recipe.
predictions.when: In fresh, rinsed-vessel repeats of the fixed 300 rpm, 60-second intervention, using the same dye bottle, locked camera, fixed addition location, common references, and alternating depth-sampling order at second 120.
predictions.result: Prediction: final depth-vial spread remains at most 4 percent even if early side-image checks exceed 4 percent. Repeated success would support dispensability of the preferred dependency in these conditions; it would not identify specks or prove that optical artifacts caused the 900 rpm fluctuations.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: the observed 300 rpm sample result was an exceptional or sampling-mediated success, and fixed lower-speed stirring generally leaves depth gradients that the preferred longer agitation would remove.
predictions.when: Under the same fresh-recipe, fixed 300 rpm, 60-second repeats with operation independent of side readings and alternating sample order.
predictions.result: Prediction: final depth-vial spread exceeds 4 percent on repeated trials; if sampling disturbance explains the earlier success, readings may also depend systematically on depth-sampling order. Failures must be recorded without adding 900 rpm or restarting to obtain optical stability. Failure of this alternative alone would not establish that 900 rpm specifically is necessary.

surviving_outcome: Already observed in one stipulated 300 rpm trial: stopping at second 60 yielded final elevation-vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent normalized spread, meeting the at-most-4-percent bounded uniformity proxy without sustained 900 rpm or its optical stop rule. This is evidence against a universal necessity claim, not proof of reliable causal sufficiency. The surviving intended outcome for the proposed repeats is three depth samples meeting that proxy at second 120 with 60 seconds of stirring; actual time savings relative to the preferred procedure remain unknown because its total stirring duration is not given. Stable side images alone cannot establish success.
unknowns: Only one successful fixed lower-speed sample trial is stipulated; repeat success is a hypothesis.
Matched final vial readings for 900 rpm are absent, so relative sample uniformity and relative stirring-time savings are undetermined.
Transient bright specks do not identify bubbles; reflections, undissolved dye and their causal effects remain unresolved.
Sampling can disturb gradients, reference repeatability is not concentration calibration, and commanded speed has no independent tachometer verification.
Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested.
